In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Puercan is the first land mammal age in the Cenozoic of North America and that it spans the K–P and early Paleocene, with the base of the age coinciding with the base of Zone 2 of the terrestrial K–P boundary and with the first appearance of the land mammals, the multituberculate Mesodma and the condylarth Cimolomys, in the Tullock Formation.
the IrZ-Coal marks the base of the Tullock, and the base of the K–P, in Garfield and eastern McCone Counties.
the IrZ-coal is the best marker of the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary and the base of the Tullock formation in the Hell Creek - Tullock area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the presence of an IrZ-Coal at the K– P boundary in the Hell Creek and Tullock formations in eastern Montana, and that the Tullock Formation contains the oldest known Puercan faunules.
we have established a new, high-resolution, and robust magnetostratigraphy for the terrestrial Cretaeous–Paleogene boundary interval in the Hell Creek and Tullock formations.
the Puercan MFA in the Hell Creek and Tullock formations in eastern Montana is defined by the first occurrence of the rodent Alphagaulus, the lagomorph Cenolophus, and the artiodactyl Hyopsodus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have a very good record of the terrestrial C–P boundary in Montana, and that the K–P mass extinction was a protracted event that lasted at least 200,000 years, and probably longer, and that the recovery of mammals was a very slow process that spanned the entire Puercan.
there is a lot of variation in the K–P transition in the Hell Creek – Tullick succession.
the Puercan is a very short interval, probably only a few hundred thousand years long.
